newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Jackson discusses street kids with Brazil leader.
newsitem.headline: Jackson discusses street kids with Brazil leader.

text.p: U.S. black leader Rev. Jesse Jackson and Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on Wednesday discussed the plight of street children and closer ties between Afro-Brazilians and African Americans.
Jackson met Cardoso before a ceremony in Brasilia's Presidential Palace marking the 301st anniversary of the death of Zumbi dos Palmares, revered as a leader of runaway slaves.
He told reporters they had spoken mainly about Brazil's street urchins, who roam the cities vulnerable to exploitation and attack by vigilante groups.
"Cardoso said the government was committed to educating street children and creating work for their parents, which in a democracy...shouldn't be too hard to do," Jackson said.

He is visiting Latin America's largest country to lend support to Brazilian black groups during a "Black Consciousness Week" centering on the remembrance of Zumbi, who led a group of escaped slaves in Brazil's interior before he was killed in an ambush in 1695.
Cardoso announced at the ceremony that he had approved a bill adding Zumbi's name to Brazil's list of national heroes.
The organisers of Jackson's week-long tour, the government-run Palmares Cultural Foundation, said it was intended to stimulate greater interchange between U.S. and Brazilian blacks.
Jackson said he told Cardoso he wanted to establish a "cultural canal" between Afro-Brazilians and African Americans. "The president said he was prepared to create such a canal," he said.
He also praised Cardoso as "a human rights visionary."
